subject: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechco.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@fintechco.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up

Hi Alex / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciated the context on FintechCo's fraud-detection roadmap and the low-latency requirements for the customer-facing risk checks. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can get you a clear cost/commit recommendation: 

Summary of deployment modes we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, usage-based billing (per-token / per-embedding). Good for pilots and variable workloads.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity (committed monthly/annual) for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. Includes SLA and isolated pools.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed networking and on-prem options for regulated workloads with strict data residency and KMS/HSM integrations.

Key signals you gave that matter for recommendation:
- Expected inference volume: ~200M tokens/month initially (grows to ~600M in 6-9 months).
- Latency SLO: 80th pct < 150ms for short prompts (<= 512 tokens).
- Data residency: US-only for production; extra compliance docs may be required.
- Security: SOC 2 + customer-managed KMS is preferred for production.

What we recommend next:
1) I'll share a simple cost-model spreadsheet with per-token vs. reserved capacity scenarios (attached).
2) If you want predictable unit economics at scale, Dedicated (reserved monthly commit) looks promising; I'll include a 12-month commit example vs hosted.
3) If you need an air-gapped on-prem option, we can outline an estimated lift-and-shift cost — Sean (cc'd) can follow up on the infra sizing assumptions.

Next steps: can you confirm the following so we can finalize the numbers?
- Typical concurrency / QPS for the risk-check endpoint (p95 and p99 if available)
- % of requests that require full-context (long prompts) vs short prompts
- Any hard constraints on outbound network or on-prem appliance needs

Attached: Redwood_Deployment_Prices.xlsx (cost model draft), MAP_Proposal_Draft.pdf (high-level commercial terms).

Happy to hop on a short follow-up to walk through the spreadsheet — I can do tomorrow between 10-12 PT.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0143
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 18:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we dig into the spreadsheet: 

1) Volume: 200M tokens/month is our alerting/monitoring path estimate. For realtime risk-check endpoint (customer-facing), we expect ~1.5k RPS peak for short prompts (~32-64 tokens) and ~150 RPS sustained. The long-context flows (1-2k tokens) are mostly batch/analytics and will be off-peak.

2) Latency: for the realtime endpoint we need 99th < 300ms and 95th < 150ms (apologies — that was my bad, those are the two SLOs we use).

3) Security: SOC 2 is table stakes; for production we need customer-managed KMS and evidence of network controls. If Dedicated meets our KMS requirement, that will likely be the route. Private/on-prem is an option but will take more procurement cycles.

Can you include a scenario:
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go) with expected per-token cost today + est month cost for 200M and 600M tokens
- Dedicated (12-month reserved) with two commit levels: medium (500 tokens/sec sustained) and high (2k tokens/sec sustained) — include approximate monthly commit and effective unit cost
- Private: ballpark one-time onboarding + recurring infra support (since we may need a ballpark for budgeting)

We can do a call tomorrow at 10:30 PT — I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
alex.turner@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechco.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fintechco.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 01:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up

Appreciate the extra detail — that helps a lot. I updated the attached spreadsheet with three scenarios per your ask and added an assumptions tab: traffic shape, average token lengths, and latency target mapping. High-level notes: 

- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token pricing in the spreadsheet is our list rate for the models we discussed. For 200M tokens it looks like ~$X/month; at 600M tokens you can see the linear cost and where a committed model becomes cost-effective.

- Dedicated (12-month reserved): I sketched two commit tiers. The medium tier covers the sustained 500 tokens/sec estimate; the high tier covers sustained 2k tokens/sec with headroom for peaks via burst policies. Committed pricing reduces your effective per-token cost ~25-40% depending on commit size.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): I included a ballpark one-time setup estimate and recurring support/ops fee. This is much higher up-front but gives full control over keys and network.

I called out areas where we need better inputs (concurrency shape, % long-context per call) — I left placeholders you can fill directly in the sheet.

I've attached the updated Redwood_Deployment_Prices.xlsx. Let me know if you want me to convert any of the scenarios into an MLP (monthly lease pricing) or a blended hybrid recommendation (Hosted for canary + Dedicated for prod).

Marissa

Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up

Alex — quick technical note from infra:

- For your realtime P95/P99 targets at the 1.5k RPS peak (short prompts), Dedicated with autoscaled GPU pools (nvlink-backed instances we discussed) should comfortably meet 95th < 150ms and 99th ~ 250-300ms depending on exact batching. We tuned assumptions to 64-token avg for the short path.
- If you go Dedicated, recommended initial config: 4x A10G nodes with continuous batching and a KV cache (prefix caching for stable prompts) — this maps to the medium commit tier in Marissa's sheet.
- For Private on-prem: we can mirror the Dedicated config but the one-time deployment work (networking, KMS integration, air-gapped images) typically adds 4-8 weeks and a higher upfront cost.

I attached a short infra assumptions snippet in the workbook. Happy to sync with your platform infra team if you want a sizing session.

—Sean
Director, Technical Solutions | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa / Sean — the spreadsheet looks good and the infra notes are helpful. Procurement looped me in and asked for a short meeting to walk the CFO through the committed vs pay-as-you-go economics. Can we do a 30-minute pricing walkthrough tomorrow? Prefer 11-12 PT.

Also: procurement asked for a simple one-slide summary of cost tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and high-level timeline for Dedicated vs Private — if you can attach that one-pager to the calendar invite that would be ideal.

I’ll confirm the calendar invite; looking forward to the walkthrough.

Alex
